responses: Machine Learning is a branch of AI where systems learn statistical patterns from data rather than following rigid rule-based programming. Paradigms include Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
Key ML concepts: Overfitting occurs when a model memorizes training noise; regularization, cross-validation, and feature scaling help generalize performance to unseen test data.
ML pipelines involve: Data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, model selection, loss minimization, and evaluation using metrics like Precision, Recall, and ROC-AUC.

responses: Deep Learning is a subset of Machine Learning utilizing multi-layered artificial neural networks (ANNs) capable of learning hierarchical feature representations directly from raw data.
In deep networks, backpropagation computes the gradient of the loss function with respect to weights using the chain rule, which optimizers like Adam use to update parameters iteratively.
Architectures like Bidirectional LSTMs process sequential data in both forward and backward directions, capturing rich bidirectional contextual dependencies ideal for text intent classification.

responses: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) converts acoustic audio signals into textual transcripts by analyzing spectrograms, extracting features like MFCCs, and mapping them through acoustic and language models.

This application uses the browser's native Web Speech API (SpeechRecognition interface), which captures audio via microphone and streams it to client/cloud ASR engines for continuous speech-to-text conversion.
Speech processing involves sampling audio waves (typically 16 kHz), performing Fourier transforms to derive frequency-domain spectrograms, and using sequence models to predict phonetic tokens.

responses: Natural Language Processing (NLP) enables computers to analyze, understand, and generate human languages. Core tasks include tokenization, POS tagging, named entity recognition, and sequence classification.
In this chatbot's NLP pipeline: raw user text is lowercased, stripped of punctuation, tokenized into integer sequence vectors, mapped to high-dimensional dense embeddings, and classified by a BiLSTM.
Word embeddings represent semantic relationships in continuous geometric vector space, where semantically similar words reside closer together by cosine distance.
